name: Permanent Residence (Immigration Act B.E. 2522)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires holding a work permit for at least 3 consecutive years, at least 1 of which with the current employer as stated in the application.
requirements.fix_path: Continue holding a valid work permit for at least 3 years, with at least the most recent year at the current employer.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires income of at least THB 80,000/month for a minimum of 2 consecutive years before submission, or alternatively personal income tax paid of at least THB 100,000/year for each of the 2 preceding years.
requirements.fix_path: Document income or personal income tax payments meeting the applicable threshold.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a minimum investment of THB 10,000,000 in Thai property, government bonds, or Thai-registered companies, with funds transferred from abroad and held for at least 3 years.
requirements.fix_path: Structure a qualifying THB 10,000,000 investment, funded from abroad and held for the required 3-year period.

requirement_groups.name: Family/humanitarian category (marriage to a Thai citizen)

requirements.blocker_text: Covers spouses and other close family members of Thai citizens with extended, documented residence in Thailand -- the specific years-of-marriage/residence threshold for this category was not independently confirmed against a primary source in this research pass.
requirements.fix_path: Confirm current family-category requirements directly with the Immigration Bureau.

evidence_required.document: 3 years' continuous Non-Immigrant visa status immediately before the application deadline
Thai-language proficiency demonstrated at the interview appointment

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: PR holders must report residence annually and notify the Immigration Bureau of address, marital-status, or employment changes within 15 days; PR is revocable for serious criminal offences, fraudulent application documents, or absence from Thailand exceeding 1 year without prior permission

sources.title: Integrity Legal -- Thai Permanent Residence: Nationality Quota Information, directly quoting the Immigration Bureau's 2022 notification setting the 100-per-nationality/50-for-stateless quota structure

LegalClarity -- Thailand Permanent Residency Requirements and Eligibility, citing the Immigration Bureau's Immigration Commission Regulation on Residential Permits for the employment-category income and work-permit thresholds
Thailand Visa -- Thailand Permanent Residency, describing the THB 10,000,000 investment-category threshold under the Immigration Act B.E. 2522

notes: STATUS: DRAFT. HONEST SOURCING GAP: no direct fetch of an Immigration Bureau (immigration.go.th) page was achieved for this route in this research pass, despite strong, specific, mutually-consistent cross-corroboration across 8+ independent sources on the core quota mechanism and category structure. STRUCTURAL FINDING, one of the most distinctively restrictive settlement routes documented anywhere in this dataset: the 100-per-nationality annual quota (not 100 total, a common misconception one source explicitly corrects) means Thai PR's real bottleneck often isn't the substantive eligibility criteria but simple arithmetic -- popular nationalities can and do exhaust their 100 slots within the roughly 2-month annual application window, meaning a fully-qualified applicant can still be shut out purely by filing order in a given year. selection_method is modeled 'merit_ranked' as the closest fit, though the actual mechanism is closer to first-come-first-served-within-quota than a true merit ranking -- flagged as an imperfect categorisation given the schema's available options. Five categories exist per the Immigration Commission's own framework (investment, employment, humanitarian/family, expert-or-academic, and extraordinary-circumstances case-by-case) -- this file models three (employment, investment, family/marriage) given sourcing depth, with the expert/academic and extraordinary-circumstances categories flagged as candidates for future expansion rather than fabricated without adequate source support. citizenship_after_months (60) reflects Nationality Act B.E. 2508 Section 10's 5-consecutive-years-of-PR requirement before naturalisation eligibility opens -- see th_naturalisation for the full downstream detail, including the distinctive points-test and National/Royal Anthem interview requirement.
